Consult Summary:
- Telemedicine consult for progressive left upper-limb numbness/tingling with possible weakness and a brief episode of left-eye visual field loss; urgent neurology referral arranged to evaluate for possible demyelinating disease.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Progressive numbness and tingling in the left arm with difficulty in fine motor tasks; brief left-eye visual disturbance.
- Timeline:
  - Boxing classes for a few weeks.
  - Left arm symptoms present for at least 2 weeks, worsening from initial tingling to more persistent numbness.
  - Transient visual disturbance in left eye (loss of part of visual field) occurred a few weeks ago, lasted ~20 minutes, resolved.
  - Recent “bad cold/flu” about a month ago lasting ~2 weeks.
- Symptom details:
  - Distribution: Left arm numbness/tingling felt from elbow into arm and hand; palmar aspect of 2nd–4th fingers affected.
  - Weakness: Denies pain-limited grip; reports difficulty hitting piano notes; can grasp a glass; weakness suspected in context of numbness.
  - Pain: Occasional shoulder pain with boxing movements; at rest primarily numbness/tingling. Right hand knuckles sore from boxing.
  - Neck pain: Patient first affirmed then denied neck pain (conflict noted).
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Shoulder discomfort with boxing movements.
  - Massage and warm baths did not improve numbness.
  - Ibuprofen taken for muscle soreness/right hand knuckle pain; not helpful for numbness.
- Associated symptoms/ROS:
  - Vision: Transient left-eye visual field loss (~20 min), resolved; no glasses/contact lens use.
  - Neurologic: No seizures/fits. Legs/walking normal.
  - Headache/fatigue: Intermittent headaches attributed by patient to fatigue/overwork; recent fatigue noted.
- Other:
  - Right-hand dominant.

Past Medical History:
- Generally healthy; no chronic medical conditions reported.
- Recent prolonged viral illness (~1 month ago) lasting ~2 weeks.
- No prior surgeries mentioned.
- Allergies: Not documented.
- Medications:
  - Ibuprofen as needed for soreness/knuckle pain; dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Vitamin D; dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Iron supplement recommended by GP, poor adherence; dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Melatonin as needed for sleep; dose/route/frequency not documented.

Social History:
- Exercise: Regular workouts; currently attending a boxing class.
- Hobbies: Plays piano.
- Work: Reports working a lot.
- Alcohol: One recent episode of heavy drinking at a social event; baseline use not detailed.
- Tobacco: Not documented.
- Recreational drugs: Not documented.

Family History:
- Father: Hypothyroidism (patient uncertain on details) and unspecified autoimmune issues.
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, hyperlipidemia.
- Neurologic conditions: None reported.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Examination findings: Not documented.

Investigations:
- None documented at this visit.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Progressive left upper-limb numbness/paresthesia with possible weakness (palmar digits 2–4; elbow to hand), occasional movement-related shoulder discomfort; not improved with conservative measures.
  - Assessment: Concerning for a neurological etiology beyond local musculoskeletal strain. Clinician discussed possibility of demyelinating disease (e.g., multiple sclerosis).
  - Plan:
    - Urgent neurology referral placed.
    - Likely need for brain imaging per neurology (“brain scan and things like that” discussed).
    - No steroids or disease-specific therapy initiated pending firm diagnosis.
    - Emergency precautions: Go to A&E/ED if weakness progresses (e.g., involves legs), new/worsening headaches, vomiting, seizures/fits, or worsening/persistent visual symptoms.
- Issue 2: Transient left-eye visual field loss (~20 minutes), resolved.
  - Plan:
    - Include in urgent neurology evaluation.
    - Same ED precautions if symptoms recur or persist.
- Issue 3: Right hand knuckle pain related to boxing.
  - Plan:
    - Patient using ibuprofen as needed; no additional management documented.

- General plan items:
  - Patient informed that early identification of conditions like MS allows treatment; patient agreed with plan.
  - Follow-up to occur after neurology assessment.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  - Allergies.
  - Vitals and focused neurological examination findings.
  - Detailed medication doses/routes/frequencies and medication reconciliation.
  - Smoking and recreational drug use history; baseline alcohol use.
  - Surgical history, immunizations, gynecologic history.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Neck pain: Patient initially said “Yes, absolutely,” then stated “No, nothing” (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality:
  - Minor hesitations/interruptions; overall understandable with adequate clinical detail for triage and referral.
